key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network integrates molecular, clinical and network data to identify and prioritize immunotherapy drug targets, and top candidates are validated using clinically relevant patient‑derived tumour explants, demonstrating translational reliability.
problem_solved: Target discovery for cancer immunotherapy is hampered by fragmented data, high false‑positive rates, and limited physiologically relevant validation; this work automates prioritization and couples predictions with ex vivo patient-derived validation to improve clinical relevance.
method: Construct a multimodal graph combining molecular (genes/proteins), functional interaction networks, and clinical features as node/edge attributes.
Train a graph neural network to classify and rank targets (approved vs prospective) and score novel candidate targets.
Experimentally validate top-ranked candidates using patient‑derived tumour explant (PDE) assays to measure target engagement and immune response ex vivo.
impact: Demonstrates a replicable AI → wet‑lab pipeline that yields clinically actionable targets; for ML practitioners it highlights the value of multimodal GNNs and pairing predictions with physiologically relevant validation to increase translational confidence.
visual_elements: Schematic multimodal graph: nodes for genes/proteins/patients and labeled edges for interactions/clinical links.
Pipeline flowchart: data modalities → GNN model → candidate ranking → PDE validation.
Comparison chart: model predictions vs approved targets and experimentally validated candidates (bar or precision/recall curves).
Illustration/photo of patient‑derived tumour explant assay with overlay of validation readouts.
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
